label: sequence started with o: late original steps (t>=3) through <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token was o, on original-phase steps from t=3 onward and on the <DEL> step (where out_tok = o is the first recall). first_tok=o accounts for 97.6% of activation mass (25x lift). Never fires at t=0-2 and essentially never in the copy phase (36 of 87792 activations). Activation ramps up over the sequence: weak at t=3 (the 1234 false positives are t=3 steps where it is still near zero), strongest mid-to-late original phase, a bit lower at <DEL>. Larger when orig(1) is also o (top examples all begin o o), but o o alone is a poor predicate. Missed activations (2.4% of mass) are small values in sequences with o at a later position (e.g. position 1) instead of position 0. Content of the current input token has little effect. Dev F1 0.91, mass recall 0.98.

issues: Secondary miss class is systematic but weak. On the test split, sequences where first_tok != o and orig(1) == o, at t in [3, L], hold 11.9% of active steps by count but only 2.1% of activation mass. The class is also unreliable as a predictor: precision is 0.14 (0.24 when restricted to t>=5). This explains the 0.84 count recall versus 0.976 mass recall. The explanation already mentions it, and adding it to the predicate makes F1 worse (0.716).
Leftover misses with o at neither position 0 nor position 1 hold 0.3% of the mass (e.g. 'f n k s s', with tiny values of 0.00-0.05). This is scattered noise.

The magnitude description is a bit off. Mean activation per active step peaks at t=4-5 (about 1.32-1.35e-5 mass per active step) and falls steadily through t=9 (1.09e-5). So it is 'early-to-mid peak, then a slow decline', not 'grows over the sequence, peaking mid-to-late'. <DEL> per active step (1.22e-5) is about the same as the original phase average (1.12e-5), not clearly lower. These are minor descriptive errors.

The 'o o' sequences (first_tok==o & orig(1)==o, t in [3, L]) hold only 4.1% of the mass, so 'top examples start with o o' is about the extreme tail only. That is consistent with the agent saying 'o o' alone is a poor predicate.

Verified claims: zero activations at t=0-2. Copy phase has 36 activations on dev; on test, t>L has recall 0.0004 and mass 0.00009. The false positives are all t=3 steps with near-zero values, and t>=4 gives precision 0.9998. Test precision is 0.983 and mass recall 0.976 as reported.
